Covariance matrix of the parameter estimates

vcov.latentmix.Rd

The robust (sandwich, Mplus MLR) covariance matrix of the estimates, rows and columns in the order of the rows of parameters() (named as by coef()). With sampling weights or a complex survey design (cluster, strata) it is design-based. Use it for Wald tests and delta-method standard errors of functions of the parameters.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'latentmix'
vcov(object, ref = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model (latentmix).

ref

For an LTA, the reference class of the multinomial logits (default K), as in parameters().

...

Unused.

Value

A numeric matrix.

Details

The matrix is singular where reported parameters are functions of others (e.g. the item-response probabilities of an item sum to 1 within class, and each probability is listed next to the threshold it derives from).

Class proportions. The parameters are the multinomial "class logit"s \(\alpha_k = \log(\pi_k / \pi_K)\), \(k < K\); the standard errors of the class proportions \(\pi = \mathrm{softmax}(\alpha_1, \dots, \alpha_{K-1}, 0)\) follow by the delta method, \(V_\pi = J V_\alpha J^\top\) with \(J = (\mathrm{diag}(\pi) - \pi\pi^\top)_{\cdot, 1:(K-1)}\), as in the example. For a model with covariates the class proportions depend on the covariates (the logits are intercepts and slopes); for a multigroup model parameters() lists the "class probability" rows with their standard errors directly.

See also

parameters(), coef.latentmix()

Examples

data(aces)
# \donttest{
m <- lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = 4)
#> Starting Julia ...
V <- vcov(m)
pt <- parameters(m)
i <- which(pt$kind == "class logit")
p <- as.vector(classprobs(m))              # class proportions
J <- (diag(p) - tcrossprod(p))[, seq_along(i)]
sqrt(diag(J %*% V[i, i] %*% t(J)))          # standard errors of the class proportions
#> [1] 0.02195626 0.01814510 0.02000563 0.01507699
# }
